title: Surprise regulatory fine on bank reputation and stock value

llm_response.content:
## 1. Identification Strategy
To assess the impact of a surprise regulatory fine on bank reputation and stock value, we will use an Event Study design. This method is suitable because it allows us to isolate the effect of the fine announcement on the stock's abnormal returns around the event date. The key assumption is that the market model, which is estimated using data from days -10 to -2 before the event, accurately captures the normal return behavior of the stock. The abnormal return (AR) is then calculated as the difference between the actual return and the expected return based on the market model. We will calculate the Cumulative Abnormal Return (CAR) over the event window [-1, +1] to determine if the fine generates negative abnormal returns beyond the direct financial cost.

## 2. R Code
```r
# Load necessary libraries
library(readr)
library(dplyr)
library(broom)

# Read the data
data <- read_csv("experiments/exp_b/data/s17_data.csv")

# Calculate abnormal returns using the market model
data <- data %>%
  group_by(stock_id) %>%
  mutate(expected_ret = beta * mkt_ret,
         ar = ret - expected_ret)

# Calculate cumulative abnormal returns (CAR) for the event window [-1, +1]
data_event_window <- data %>%
  filter(event_day >= -1 & event_day <= 1)

car_data <- data_event_window %>%
  group_by(stock_id) %>%
  summarise(car = sum(ar))

# Calculate the fine ratio (fine/mktcap) average
fine_ratio_avg <- mean(data$fine_ratio, na.rm = TRUE)

# Print the average CAR and compare it to the average fine ratio
cat("Average CAR:", mean(car_data$car, na.rm = TRUE), "\n")
cat("Average Fine Ratio:", fine_ratio_avg, "\n")

# Check if CAR < -fine_ratio on average
if (mean(car_data$car, na.rm = TRUE) < -fine_ratio_avg) {
  cat("Reputational damage beyond the fine itself is suggested.\n")
} else {
  cat("No reputational damage beyond the fine itself is suggested.\n")
}
```

## 3. Expected Findings
We expect the average Cumulative Abnormal Return (CAR) to be negative, indicating that the surprise regulatory fine announcement generates negative abnormal returns. If the magnitude of the CAR is greater than the average fine ratio (in absolute terms), it would suggest that there is reputational damage beyond the direct financial cost of the fine. The sign and magnitude of the CAR will depend on how investors perceive the fine and its implications for the bank's future performance and reputation. A larger negative CAR would indicate more severe reputational damage.

_ground_truth.conclusion_detail: CAR exceeds fine/mktcap ratio, confirming reputational damage beyond monetary penalty
_ground_truth.main_effect: CAR ≈ −3.5%; reputational component ≈ −1.5% above direct cost
